races.name: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: River Jordan
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who lacks the pace to naturally close from the rear over five furlongs when Palm Reader controls a steady tempo; two runs yielding a fifth and seventh on Good ground suggest modest ability, and 21 days since last run is straightforward.|

runners_data.name: Unbeatable Fame
runners_data.note: Only one run to her name — a seventh over this trip on Good ground — leaving her profile almost entirely open; Fahey's yard is in decent form (1/45 over 14 days) and she cannot be dismissed on ability grounds, but the style is unknown and the experience gap is real.|

runners_data.name: Suenicora Star
runners_data.note: Sole run was a distant twelfth over six furlongs on Standard turf, which gives almost nothing to work with; hold-up tag combined with a tendency to fade in the finish is a double liability in a race where Palm Reader may not generate enough early pace to suit closers.|

runners_data.name: Bacha
runners_data.note: Fahey's other runner here; a true hold-up horse whose natural rearward position has been compressed into midfield on the map because the field's rear is already crowded — meaning it will not get the settling room it needs and its finishing effort may be blunted accordingly. A fifth on Standard at five furlongs is modest form.|

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.note: Two runs on Good ground producing a third and a second show this Kevin Ryan juvenile is competitive and tactically versatile; an unknown-style tag suggests it can slot in wherever the gaps appear, and its placed form makes it the most battle-tested hold-up/prominent type in the field after Palm Reader.|

runners_data.name: Red Blue Point
runners_data.note: Debutant from James Tate's yard, which has the second-best recent trainer strike rate in this field (1/13 over 14 days); De Sousa is a high-quality booking and first-time runners from this operation often arrive fit, but going suitability is genuinely unknown, making this a watch rather than a lean.|

runners_data.name: Palm Reader
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over five furlongs, races prominently — here it is the lone confirmed pace-setter — and runs in headgear; Declan Carroll's stable is in form (1/7 over 14 days) and, absent any pace rival, this horse holds a structurally commanding role in the race shape.|

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse nudged into a midfield mapping because rear slots are oversubscribed; form of eighth and fifth on Good ground at five furlongs is modest, and William Pyle's claim means this is a rider-at-level booking, though the Frost yard is genuinely in form (3/13 over 14 days).|

races.paceDynamic: Palm Reader is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will coast into a comfortable, uncontested position from the gates and dictate a sustainable gallop over Thirsk's flat five furlongs. With Good ground and a clean lead, Palm Reader can control tempo, avoiding the gruelling early burn that would ordinarily set up closers, making this a race likely run at a measured, even pace rather than a searching one. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Bacha and Articulate are genuine hold-up horses but have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning true cover and separation behind the pace will be compressed rather than spread. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader dictating a fair but not extreme gallop on Good turf — strongly favours horses who can track prominently and pounce in the final furlong, with pure hold-up runners at a disadvantage given the lack of a fast pace to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Palm Reader Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Palm Reader is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the break and set a sustainable, even gallop that suits its natural rhythm.
scenarios.body: Palm Reader won on Good ground over this exact trip and carries headgear, and with no rival willing or able to push it early, it can conserve energy and sprint clear when asked in the final furlong. Horses with prominent or tracking styles who can latch on within striking range are the most dangerous, but a wire-to-wire win is the dominant shape here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Palm Reader sets just enough pace that a horse tracking in second or third can wear it down and pick it off close home.
scenarios.body: Battle Fever has placed twice on Good ground and has the tactical speed to sit handy and challenge in the final 100 yards, while Red Blue Point is a well-regarded unknown who could benefit from a prominent position under De Sousa.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If Palm Reader's gallop is faster than it appears early, stringing the field out and creating enough of a pace to allow hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: River Jordan and Bacha are genuine hold-up types, but the measured pace expected here will blunt their finishing kick; they need more fractions than Palm Reader is likely to provide on this flat, speed-favouring track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the race is tactically muddled by unexpected pace injection from an unknown or lightly raced runner, scrambling the anticipated shape.
scenarios.body: Unbeatable Fame and Red Blue Point are both lightly raced unknowns whose true ability and racing pattern remain untested in a shape context; either could outrun their current price if they find an unexpectedly strong tactical position.

watchPoints.text: Palm Reader's reaction at the start is critical — if it misses the break, no other confirmed front runner replaces it and the race shape collapses entirely into a muddling, compressed midfield sprint.

Bacha and Articulate are both natural hold-up horses forced into midfield; watch for them to drift wide seeking clear air in the final two furlongs, potentially causing interference or checking rivals on a narrow five-furlong straight.

Red Blue Point's debut for James Tate with De Sousa in the saddle merits close monitoring in the market — any significant gamble would suggest stable confidence and upgrade this runner's scenario probability materially.

Battle Fever's two prior runs were on Good ground, both resulting in placings, making it the only runner outside Palm Reader with verifiable form in conditions that match today exactly — worth tracking through the first half for how fluently it travels.|

races.name: William Hill Summer Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has winning form on soft and was runner-up at 7f on good last time; he sets the pace here but his STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is racing slightly out of natural role, which tempers confidence if pressured late.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's five-year-old won over 10f on good ground and has strong course-type form, but drops sharply in trip to a mile and steps up significantly in class; trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/3 is not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' eight-year-old has course-and-distance experience and won over 7f on good last time out; prominent style is ideally suited to this moderate-pace scenario and his trainer sends runners out in strong form (T14: 6/25).

runners_data.name: Pure Legend
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old won at 7f on soft but has a concern on similar going — only 1 placing from 11 comparable efforts — and is race-fresh after 69 days; prominent style fits the race shape but the good ground record is thin.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's seven-year-old is a hold-up type whose recent form string (890000) shows a horse badly out of form; trainer strike rate over 14 days is strong (12/59) but this horse needs a strong pace to produce a finish, which is unlikely here.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's four-year-old drops back from 12f trips and switches from heat to turf; hold-up style needs a genuine gallop and the step down in trip is an obvious query — showed a 5f good-ground placing but overall flat-mile profile is unproven.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's seven-year-old is genuinely a prominent racer by nature, flagged to finish with a fade, but with more pace types than the race can accommodate he is likely to find himself further back than ideal; his sim-going record of 10 runs without a win in this competitive band is a concern.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's five-year-old has placed second over this course and distance on good, making him one of the most course-relevant entries; prominent style suits the expected race shape and Cam Hardie's local knowledge adds a small tactical edge.

runners_data.name: Dosman
runners_data.note: Oli Rix's five-year-old has won over this trip on standard and has placed consistently, but his natural front-running tendencies are squeezed by the field's pace surplus — he will likely race further off the pace than his best form demands, weighing against his chance.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's seven-year-old won over this course and distance on good ground recently and brings back-to-back placed efforts at this trip; hold-up style is a small disadvantage in a slow-pace scenario but a genuine finisher if the gallop quickens late.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's four-year-old has won back-to-back over a mile on good ground and holds strong recent form; his hold-up style is the key caveat in what looks a moderate-pace race, but he is the most in-form closer in the field if any late surge materialises.

runners_data.name: Jeddaal
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old won at a mile on soft and has placed over this trip on good, but his natural prominent style cannot be fully expressed with the field's pace competition — George Downing will need to make tactical decisions early that may compromise his run.

races.paceDynamic: Fondo Blanco is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press hard from the outset, he should control tempo from a flat, uncontested position through the early and middle portions of this mile. The pace is likely to be honest but measured — a single leader dictating on good ground over Thirsk's flat mile typically produces a true-run race that does not stretch hold-up horses but equally does not hand anything away for free. Runners who can travel prominently in behind Fondo Blanco — specifically Northern Express and Mr Swivell — are best placed to exploit a sustainable gallop by launching controlled challenges from two furlongs out rather than having to make up ground from deep. This shape plainly favours prominent-to-midfield types who can sit within two lengths of the pace and pounce; genuine closers tracking from the rear will find the tempo insufficient to set up a late swoop. It must be noted that this field carries significantly more prominent pace than can all find their natural position: Mirsky, Dosman, and Jeddaal are true prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled further back than ideal, compromising their ability to deliver from the position they prefer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fondo Blanco Controls, Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Fondo Blanco sets a measured, uncontested lead and prominent trackers close smoothly from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Fondo Blanco's controlled front-running produces a true but not scorching pace, allowing Northern Express and Mr Swivell to sit ideally placed and challenge on their terms from the two-furlong pole. Prominent types who travel without cover problems claim the first slots as hold-up horses lack the late sectional to overhaul them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is genuinely slow and Fondo Blanco builds an unassailable lead that rivals cannot close.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Fondo Blanco slows the race to a dawdle and then kicks away from the front before chasers organise; Roger Varian's horse has the class and a recent win to suggest he can sustain if given a soft lead. Hold-up types who need a strong pace to produce their best finish are stranded, and only the best-positioned prominent trackers have any realistic chance of pegging him back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace is faster than expected — perhaps through early jostling from the many prominent types — and Fondo Blanco's lead stretches the field, leaving closers with ground to make up but a proper gallop to aim at.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end pace would tire the prominent brigade and open the door for Sterling Knight or Priapos, both hold-up types with good recent form on good ground over this trip. Priapos in particular brings back-to-back wins and a profile that thrives when a strong pace sets up a meaningful late surge at Thirsk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Unexpected Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types creates early crowding, burning off pace and causing multiple position changes that scramble the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: Redistribution of Mirsky, Dosman, and Jeddaal away from their natural prominent slots means at least one will be caught in traffic or forced wide; a chaotic mid-race reshuffle could open the door for an unfancied runner to creep into a winning position at a big price. Pure Legend, stepping up in class but race-fresh after 69 days, or Sterling Knight hunting back-to-back wins could be the beneficiary in a muddled contest.

watchPoints.text: Fondo Blanco's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the central race factor — watch whether any of the surplus prominent types (Mirsky, Dosman, Jeddaal) push up to press him early, which would dramatically change the pace shape.

Priapos brings the hottest recent form in the race (back-to-back wins) but is a hold-up type in a likely slow-pace contest — watch how Oisin McSweeney positions him in the first two furlongs to judge whether he can get competitive.

Northern Express is eight years old but arrives with course form and a recent win; watch his position at the two-furlong marker — if he is within two lengths of Fondo Blanco at that point, his prominent profile gives him a clear chance.

Pure Legend's 69-day absence and poor record on comparable good ground are worth monitoring in the market — any significant drift from his morning price would reinforce going concerns, while a firm move would suggest stable confidence regardless.

The three redistributed prominent runners (Mirsky, Dosman, Jeddaal) all carry STYLE_FIT discounts — if any drifts markedly in the market it may signal connections are aware their horse cannot secure the position its form demands.

races.name: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Le Samourai
runners_data.note: Won on debut at 7f at Salisbury (Good to Soft), stepping up to a mile here with Ralph Beckett — a trainer who excels developing milers — and Edward Greatrex aboard; sits naturally prominent and is ideally positioned to track Regal Desire throughout before launching a challenge in the straight.

runners_data.name: Morty Robinson
runners_data.note: Experienced six-year-old whose sole recent run produced a 13th-place finish over 7f at Salisbury; a true hold-up horse by style, though the field's composition forces him into a midfield berth he would not naturally choose, and the ⚠ fade flag raises stamina concerns in any case.

runners_data.name: Ben Travato
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison runner who finished sixth on his most recent start over 7f at Goodwood on Good ground — the closest sim-going comparison yields no wins or places; instinctively suited to coming from off the pace, though the race map places him ahead of his comfort zone given the cluster of closers in this field.

runners_data.name: Test Run
runners_data.note: Ran fourth and fifth in his two starts at 8f (Good and Soft) and is one of the genuine hold-up types who will settle at the back; the Michael & David Easterby yard has shown recent form (3/32 in 14 days) but Test Run has yet to win or place, and making ground from the rear against a controlled front-end pace is a structural challenge.

runners_data.name: West Sleekburn Lad
runners_data.note: Returns after a 57-day break for Peter Niven having finished 8th and 10th in his two runs — both on Good ground at longer trips — carrying the ⚠ fade flag and zero wins or places from two sim-going starts; the layoff plus poor form profile makes this a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Brighton Beach
runners_data.note: William Haggas, Daniel Tudhope, and a placed effort (3rd, 10f, Good) give this horse the strongest credentials among the hold-up group; instinctively a hold-up type who is displaced into midfield by the field's composition, though Haggas's horses regularly adapt tactically and Brighton Beach's two Good-ground efforts suggest the going is no concern.

runners_data.name: Regal Desire
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner with two runner-up finishes over 8f (Good and Standard) for Brian Ellison; the STYLE_FIT tag notes it may be racing slightly out of its most comfortable role, but with zero pace pressure from any rival, Regal Desire will effectively dictate every aspect of how this mile unfolds.

races.paceDynamic: Regal Desire is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful pace pressure from any rival, will stride into an uncontested lead from the off and set a controlled, sustainable gallop over Thirsk's flat mile. Le Samourai is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and will likely sit just behind Regal Desire, leaving the remainder — Morty Robinson, Brighton Beach, and Ben Travato — shuffled into midfield despite being genuine hold-up types, simply because the field has too many closers to all find their natural rear position. Test Run and West Sleekburn Lad are authentic hold-up horses who will settle at the back, but with the pace controlled and modest, making ground from deep may prove difficult in a race where the tempo is unlikely to generate a true end-to-end test. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently — Regal Desire leading and Le Samourai close up are ideally placed to capitalise on a front-end-dominated contest where late runners face a stiff ask against a measured, dictated gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Regal Desire Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Desire sets an uncontested, measured pace and the field fails to apply pressure at any stage of the mile.
scenarios.body: Regal Desire dictates every yard from a clean break, while Le Samourai tracks closely in second and the hold-up brigade are left with too much ground to make up from midfield and rear. Front-end prominence is rewarded as the controlled gallop denies closers a true end-of-race surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and genuine closers find enough momentum from the rear to overhaul the leaders.
scenarios.body: Test Run or West Sleekburn Lad — the truest hold-up types — would need Regal Desire to have stolen too far ahead early and then tire in the final furlong, opening a window for late challengers. This shape requires a moderate-to-fast early pace that burns out the front-runners, which is structurally unlikely given no real pressure exists.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses adapt quickly to their unnatural midfield position and produce a strong sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Brighton Beach, with the strongest recent form figures among the hold-up group and Haggas's saddling, is best placed to benefit if the pace quickens early enough to spread the field. Ben Travato would need to overcome inexperience and racing against his natural instinct, making this a lower-probability scenario dependent on multiple horses performing out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Le Samourai Leads Late
scenarios.trigger: If Le Samourai improves significantly on debut win and overpowers Regal Desire in the final furlong after tracking throughout.
scenarios.body: Le Samourai's recent win at 7f suggests stamina for the mile is not guaranteed, though the Ralph Beckett yard is respected for patient mile development. A strong closing display from the prominent position is plausible only if Regal Desire overcooks the pace — an unlikely outcome given the controlled dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Regal Desire — watch for a clean break and immediate lead; if it establishes an uncontested lead within the first furlong with no rival willing to press, it becomes very difficult to pass on a flat track with a controlled tempo.

Brighton Beach — Daniel Tudhope is a top-level jockey who may position this hold-up type more aggressively than expected; watch whether Tudhope allows Brighton Beach to travel in midfield with cover rather than trailing the field, which would improve its chance markedly.

Le Samourai — keep an eye on whether it gets a comfortable position just behind Regal Desire from stall draw; if it gets squeezed or loses its pitch early, its chance of tracking and pouncing is compromised given its limited racecourse experience.

Morty Robinson and West Sleekburn Lad — both carry ⚠ fade flags and both are true hold-up types pushed into midfield; if the pace is slow they are unlikely to find the finish they need, and their combined presence in midfield could create traffic issues for Brighton Beach and Ben Travato turning for home.

Test Run and West Sleekburn Lad — the two authentic rear-of-field closers; monitor how quickly the pace develops from the front, as only a genuinely strong early tempo would give these two any realistic chance of covering the ground required over Thirsk's flat mile finish.

races.name: Jordan Foy Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: Veteran 9-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent form includes a second from off the pace on good at this trip, but T14 record of 0/11 is a serious negative and he will be even further from the action than ideal in a field this packed with closers.

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with a win on good ground over this course and distance in her last five, trained by Furtado who is 4/23 in the past fortnight; her natural style is to come from the back but with so many similar types in the field she may have to settle for midfield rather than a rearward berth.

runners_data.name: Muker
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a modest recent sequence of 800640 who favours dropping in and finishing off, yet his last 12 runs on good turf show just 2 wins and 3 places — the redistribution into midfield suits him no worse than his natural position given he rarely gets competitive runs from deep anyway.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing mare for Tim Easterby who is fresh off a win on soft last time and has strong each-way form on good, wearing a hood; she is likely to be one of the horses to actually secure the prominent pitch and track True Promise closely.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type on a poor run of form (281409) with no wins from his last seven outings on good ground; Bryan Smart yard has had a quiet fortnight at 0/4 and nothing in his profile shouts for this track and going combination.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's six-year-old carries the most compelling recent form in the race — three wins from 11 efforts on good, a latest-run second here at Thirsk — and his prominent racing style makes him the natural beneficiary if True Promise's tempo is anything less than perfect.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr hold-up runner whose recent form is patchy (5U5305), has no recent good-ground form in his history, and the reality is he will be jostling for a midfield slot rather than his ideal position well off the pace in a field saturated with similar types.

runners_data.name: Comic Strip
runners_data.note: Young Simon and Ed Crisford three-year-old wearing a tongue-strap, racing hold-up, but his form on genuinely good turf is very limited (only 2 runs sim-going, 0W 0P); 33 days between runs and an inexperienced profile suggest he is vulnerable in this company.

runners_data.name: True Promise
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner — Fionn McSharry sends him here after a Sligo win last year, but good-ground form (sim-going: 3/15, 0W 1P) is a concern, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder that if this pace shape is taken away from him he has few options; everything depends on getting the lead cheaply.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: George Scott's six-year-old has a strong recent record on good ground (8/15, 1W 4P) and finished second over 6f good last time; held-up by nature and Kevin Stott gives him every chance of being positioned just off the main midfield pack where a clean run could count.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old is the best-matched horse in the field on similar going (13/15 sim-going, 2W 6P) and Daniel Tudhope is a significant booking; a hold-up style with genuine tactical awareness from Tudhope means he is one of the more interesting prospects if pace materialises ahead of him.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's second runner is a natural hold-up horse, but with so many closers in the field his jockey Jack Callan will likely find himself nearer midfield than he would want; his one good-ground win came over 5f and he showed a second recently, making him capable if a cleaner position emerges.

races.paceDynamic: True Promise is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other natural leader to press her, she is expected to stride into an uncontested lead and control tempo on her own terms over this flat 5f at Thirsk. Rock Of England and Canaria Queen are the most likely prominent horses to track closely, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a helter-skelter gallop. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Mondammej, Rotokura Belle, Muker, Accrual, American Bay and Moulin Booj are all genuine come-from-behind horses, but because there are far more of them than the map can accommodate at the rear, several will be shuffled forward into midfield positions that are not truly their role; of those, Rotokura Belle, American Bay and Accrual are best placed to actually secure a closer tracking position. A controlled, honest gallop on good ground over a flat sprint favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — the true deep closers will find it hard to generate enough momentum to overhaul a leader allowed to dictate completely, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the one to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: True Promise Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If True Promise bowls into the lead unopposed and sets a measured, controlled tempo that suits her stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: True Promise dictates every yard on her own terms, slowing the pace to a level that maximises her chance of lasting home, and horses tracking off a solo leader on flat Thirsk turf rarely get closer as the race develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of England or Canaria Queen press True Promise hard enough from the outset to compromise her reserves.
scenarios.body: A competitive but not brutal pace develops with two or three horses in close contention, meaning the leader ties up late and one of the handy trackersfinds the extra gear to cut her down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns genuinely honest and True Promise is taken on sufficiently to open ground for a closer.
scenarios.body: A brisk early tempo strings the field out and the best of the midfield gallopers — those with strong good-ground form at the trip — find the rail or a gap to charge through in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the race evolves into a strongly-run dash that completely burns off the prominent runners, leaving room for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: This requires an unusually hot pace for a handicap with one front-runner, making it the least likely shape, and several of the supposed hold-up runners are redistribued types unlikely to be in their ideal position anyway.

watchPoints.text: True Promise's early lead — if Canaria Queen or Rock Of England push the gallop rather than settle, True Promise's stamina over 5f good ground could be fully tested and the entire race shape shifts.

Tiva's draw and position — with Daniel Tudhope aboard and the best similar-going record in the field, watch if he gets a clean passage through the midfield pack; he is capable of finishing strongly if not boxed in.

Rock Of England's starting position — Thirsk's flat, straight 5f means draw and early position are significant; if he can slot into second or third from the gate he is ideally positioned to challenge the leader inside the final furlong.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Mondammej, Muker, Accrual, American Bay) who cannot all get their preferred rear position may cause trouble in running as they jostle for space in the early-mid furlong, particularly if the pace is not honest enough to string them out naturally.

Rotokura Belle's yard form — Ivan Furtado is 4/23 in the past fortnight, and at 3 years old on a track she has won at before, if she manages to secure a genuinely forward position despite her natural style, she could outrun expectations.

races.name: William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: A six-year-old with extensive good-ground 7f form (0W2P in similar going), Kevin Stott retains the ride for Edward Bethell who is firing at 2/25 in the last fortnight; prominent style suits this controlled pace shape and he ran respectably here last month.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa picks up the ride for a yard with limited recent form (0/2 in 14 days), but Croupier's record of three wins and five places on similar going is a standout positive, and two of those wins came over this exact trip on good ground.

runners_data.name: Asuka
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Jack Callan claims 3lb for George Boughey who is in form (3/23 T14); two wins from three starts on good ground including a recent Yarmouth success over 6f underlines the ability, and dictating terms at her own pace is a massive advantage in this field.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Hasn't run in 57 days which is the longest absence in this field, but Archie Watson's yard has the tools to have a horse ready; good-ground form is solid (1W2P in 10 runs) and she placed at this trip on good going last summer, racing prominently as usual.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old wears a hood and is held up prominently by nature, but her recent form figures of 166764 show she has been finding opponents too strong; five runs on similar going without a placing here is a concern for confidence.

runners_data.name: Yankee Dude
runners_data.note: Returning from 117 days off — longest gap in this field — for Warren Greatrex who has only 1/10 in the last fortnight; two wins on Tapeta and one placing at 7f on good ground but the layoff and minimal trainer form tempers expectations despite a prominent racing style.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and carries good-ground experience (2W2P from 15 similar-going runs), with a last-time-out win that looks the key positive; races prominently and the Richard Fahey/Peter Fahey operation are 1/45 recently which puts a dampener on stable form.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up specialist has a 1-2 in recent form which is eye-catching, and the trainer is busy (6/88 T14); the worry is whether Asuka's measured pace will be fast enough to set up a closing run from the rear over flat Thirsk terrain.

runners_data.name: New Image
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old has a strong record on similar going (2W4P) and is a natural front-of-the-pack racer by inclination, but in this prominent-heavy field he is likely to find his early position compromised and will need to find a run from deeper than ideal.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner for Mark Walford who is 4/17 in T14, and an excellent placed record (1W6P) at 7-8f on good ground; naturally wants to race prominently, but the congested early order in this field means he may not access that role, which tempers his chance unless he breaks smartly.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old wears a tongue-strap and a cheekpiece combination and has placed second twice from recent starts; a hold-up horse with a reasonable good-ground record (1W4P), though his closing efforts will depend on the pace being strong enough from Asuka.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — his recent 5-5-1-12-9 form pattern over 7-8f on good ground supports caution; Julie Camacho's yard is quiet (0/16 T14) and his hold-up style faces the twin obstacles of a controlled pace and a tendency to empty late.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley rides for a decent-form Michael Dods yard (6/25); has a win at 8f on good ground and placed three times from similar conditions, though switching down to 7f is fine given his speed; genuine hold-up horse who needs gaps to open on the flat Thirsk straight.

runners_data.name: King's School
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's five-year-old wears a tongue-strap and cheekpiece combination and won last time on Tapeta; good-ground form here is minimal (0W1P from 2 runs) which is a genuine concern, and a hold-up style on a flat track with a controlled pace is a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old wears a visor and has returned to form with a sequence of placed efforts (5 places from 12 similar-going runs), but races frequently (7d since last run); though he wants to be up with the pace by nature, the prominent glut in this field pushes him back and he will need luck in running.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's lowest-rated runner (OR=72) has a poor recent form string of 556680 with no wins or places on good ground from six similar-going starts; a true hold-up horse in a race where closers face an uphill task against a controlled pace, and her chance looks slim on all evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Asuka is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine gate-to-wire type in the field, is positioned to control this race at a sustainable pace from the off over Thirsk's flat 7f. Yorkshire, Aurora Majesty, Croupier, Angel Hunter, Our Havana and Yankee Dude all carry prominent credentials but must battle for early position behind the leader, creating a bunched early-order chase pack rather than a true pace war — Asuka's tempo will be honest but not searingly fast. The hold-up horses — Brighton Boy, Andesite, Obelix, Glenfinnan and King's School — will be ridden for their natural finish from off the pace, but on a flat track with a controlled gallop they need pace to be fully honest to maximise their run. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their preferred position: New Image, It Just Takes Time and Woodstock are genuine prominently-raced horses forced back in the map, and of those three, It Just Takes Time's recent form (1-2-2) and New Image's class give them the best chance of actually tracking up early if gaps allow; Woodstock's visor adds an X-factor but he faces similar congestion. This race shape — a single front-runner dictating a genuine but not brutal pace — favours horses racing prominently or just off the leader, with enough run to the line to hold off closers on a flat, fair track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Asuka Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Asuka leads cleanly at a steady-to-honest gallop and the horses racing in her slipstream get the softest possible passage.
scenarios.body: Asuka sets fractions that suit those just behind her, with Yorkshire, Croupier and Aurora Majesty best-placed to pounce in the final 2f as the pace holds true on good ground at Thirsk.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pack behind Asuka races keenly and the pace lifts from the halfway point, turning it into a test of sustained galloping speed.
scenarios.body: Croupier and Yorkshire, both with strong good-ground records at this trip, are ideally positioned to run Asuka down in the final furlong as the tempo rises and the race becomes a stamina-tinged sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If Asuka and the prominent horses burn themselves out enough to leave a meaningful gap for closers to exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Brighton Boy, Andesite and Glenfinnan all have the tactical speed to close strongly if the pace proves honest enough, with Brighton Boy's recent 1-2 form making him the most dangerous of the late finishers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Upset
scenarios.trigger: If New Image or It Just Takes Time manage to break sharply and secure a prominent pitch early, racing in their natural role rather than the midfield slot the map forces on them.
scenarios.body: It Just Takes Time's last-time-out win and sequence of placed efforts at 7-8f on good ground give him the profile to exploit a front-tracking position if the prominent group fans wide and leaves a rail-side slot; New Image is the each-way wildcard if David O'Meara's charge travels sweetly just off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Asuka's early sections will define the whole race — if Jack Callan allows a completely unchallenged lead with a slow first half, the horses racing just behind her (Yorkshire, Croupier, Aurora Majesty) will be coiled and very hard to pass in the straight.

New Image, It Just Takes Time and Woodstock are natural prominent racers all forced into midfield by the congested early order — watch the first furlong for any of them breaking sharply and trying to reclaim their true position, which would suddenly increase the pace and change the race shape entirely.

It Just Takes Time ran only 12 days ago and Woodstock only 7 days ago — short turnarounds in a 16-runner handicap over 7f on good ground can lead to freshness issues or, conversely, fitness advantages; watch them in the betting for market clues.

Obelix is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish despite winning at this trip — if he is prominent in the straight at the 2f marker, he represents a horse likely to be swallowed up by those finishing more strongly, and his rivals can take confidence from that tendency.

Aurora Majesty's 57-day layoff is the longest in the field — if Archie Watson's yard has had her spot-on, the fact she is returning fresh to a trip and going she has won on (1W2P, 7f, good) could make her dangerous; watch her in the pre-race market.

races.name: Vision Pvc Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with strong course-relevant sim-going record (7 runs, 1W3P on Good), De Sousa's booking is a clear positive, and five runs over 12-14f this season suggest the trip holds no fears — the chief danger is the dawdling pace negating his staying asset.|

runners_data.name: Northern Brave
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old whose best form has come over shorter trips (8f) and on softer ground, so 1m4f on Good at Thirsk is both a trip and a going step into the unknown after 43 days off — Beasley is a valuable booking on a track-sensitive circuit.|

runners_data.name: La Peregrina
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has placed twice at 12-14f on Good ground and is comfortably the most progressive shape in the field, but she is a genuine hold-up horse whose style makes her reliant on a true run; in a race where the entire field shares her sit-and-finish instinct, she may find herself trapped without a clear lead to chase.|

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old has worn a hood (hg:p) and has a consistent but winless profile over 8-12f on Good, with five successive Good-ground runs showing no inclination to improve from the rear — at OR 69 carrying 128lbs, he is the lowest-rated runner and his STYLE_FIT flag underlines the risk of backing him in a race where his preferred tactical position may not materialise.|

races.paceDynamic: All four runners are hold-up types, meaning no horse is likely to volunteer for the lead and the early gallop at 1m4f on good ground at Thirsk will almost certainly be pedestrian and reluctant. With no genuine front-runner in the field, the pace will drift along in a tight, slowly-run bunch before one horse forces the issue turning for home, compressing the race into a sprint-finish over the final two furlongs. La Peregrina and That Darn Cantor are genuine hold-up horses displaced into the midfield position on the map purely because the entire field shares that profile — neither will race any further forward than their natural inclination allows, and both are effectively racing out of role in any scenario that demands positional flexibility. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse with the sharpest finishing kick and the best form over this trip at this end of the handicap, as the compressed, slowly-run nature of the race will place a premium on late acceleration rather than stamina or tactical nous.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dawdle Then Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early stages and a sharp two-furlong dash off slow fractions decides the race.
scenarios.body: The tight pack creeps around Thirsk's flat circuit before someone kicks off the home turn, turning this 1m4f contest into a sprint; horses with proven finishing speed over shorter trips or those who handle a compressed finish benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Suits Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If one runner is bounced along or the field collectively sets a genuine medium pace that rewards true stamina.
scenarios.body: A more honest tempo stretches the field out and allows the horse with the most genuine staying credentials to grind clear in the final furlong rather than sprinting; form over 1m4f+ in similar conditions becomes the critical factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Youth And Freshness Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the younger three-year-olds benefit from lower weights and a compact, late-finishing race that masks experience gaps.
scenarios.body: The compressed finish neutralises Ludo's Landing's course-and-distance experience and the lighter burdens on the three-year-olds give them a natural advantage in the closing stages; a horse with an unexposed profile over this trip could outfinish the older rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At Front Gifts Race
scenarios.trigger: If confusion over the lead causes erratic pace swings, pockets, and traffic problems that allow one horse to thread through late.
scenarios.body: A messy race with no willing leader produces checking, bunching, and gaps opening unpredictably; the horse drawn widest or ridden most patiently avoids trouble and picks up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a false start or very slow early gallop — with no willing leader among Ludo's Landing, Northern Brave, La Peregrina, and That Darn Cantor, the field could crawl for the first half-mile, making in-running position and the draw for the home straight critical.

La Peregrina is a natural hold-up horse mapped out of her comfort zone — if she cannot find clear daylight two furlongs out, her finishing effort could be physically blocked in a compressed four-runner dash.

Northern Brave's last run was 43 days ago and his best form is over 8f on softer ground; if the compact sprint-finish rewards fitness and trip-proven horses, his layoff and inexperience at 1m4f become compounding risks.

Silvestre De Sousa on Ludo's Landing is the standout jockey booking — De Sousa's record at Thirsk and his ability to deliver a hold-up horse with a perfectly timed run in a sprint finish could prove the decisive factor in a compressed race.

That Darn Cantor's headgear (hood, previously worn) is worth monitoring at the stalls — if the horse is unsettled pre-race or dwells at the break, losing ground in a tiny four-runner field could be terminal in a race already dominated by hold-up styles.

races.name: John Joseph Robson Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7-year-old has been running through the field in a hold-up role on good turf, going 0W1P from 9 similar-ground runs, but the absence of genuine pace-setters means he lands on the lead entirely out of character — a style-fit concern that tempers confidence, though Easterby knows how to place older sprinters tactically.

runners_data.name: Fanjove
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 3-year-old holds only 0W0P from 2 runs on comparable going, and has raced exclusively at 6-7f on flat, standard tracks; though mapped to midfield here, his natural game is to come from well off the pace, which is compromised in a steadily-run race where that ground will not be given back.

runners_data.name: Lord Abama
runners_data.note: Michael Dods has placed this 7-year-old consistently over 6f on good turf (1W3P from 10 relevant runs), and Billy Garritty has a workable relationship with the yard, but the horse's deepest-closing tendencies are squeezed by the moderate tempo — his chance relies on late gaps that may not materialise at Thirsk's flat six.

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-strap for Brian Ellison, this 4-year-old has a 0W1P record from 6 similar-going runs and has finished 3rd-4th-4th across recent 6f starts — solid but not a finisher who thrives when the gallop is falsely steady; Ben Robinson may struggle to find daylight late if the field fans wide.

runners_data.name: Khabib
runners_data.note: Ray Craggs' veteran 8-year-old brings four placed efforts on good ground and has 0W4P from 10 comparable runs, suggesting he hits the board regularly but can't land the blow — carrying 136lbs and coming back from 46 days off adds further doubt, and Cian Horgan's 5lb claim only partly offsets those concerns.

runners_data.name: Mecca's Symphony
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this Michael Dods 4-year-old who has her best form at 7f on good ground (0W3P from 8 relevant runs), dropping back to 6f here where she is racing slightly shorter than ideal; her true style is to come late, and in a race where the pace is gentle, the shortened trip and modest tempo work against her.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride for Ross Burdon on this 6-year-old who has 2W3P from 8 good-ground runs including a win over 7f and a 4th over this exact 6f trip on good; the visor goes on and De Sousa's ability to position horses quietly in a compact field makes Northcliff the most tactically flexible runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's 4-year-old arrives just 12 days after winning over this 6f trip on good ground, and his 2W3P record from 11 similar-going runs confirms he handles the conditions well; Jonathan England on board keeps it in-house, and a horse who won off OR 65 recently is right at the right mark — freshness from a quick turnaround is the only question.

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 5-year-old returns after just 10 days and arrives with a 2nd and a 1st in recent outings over 6-7f on good turf, recording 1W2P from 11 similar-going runs; wearing a hood and ridden by Cam Hardie who knows him well, he is drawn to race positionally and his late kick off a moderate pace looks a live threat.

races.paceDynamic: Bay Breeze is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front despite being a natural hold-up horse, meaning this 6f at Thirsk is likely to be run at a controlled, honest but uncontested gallop with no rival pressing Bay Breeze for the lead. The absence of a genuine front-runner creates a moderate, sustainable tempo rather than a breakneck early pace, which compresses the field and reduces the advantage for deep closers. Northcliff, Great, and Kings Merchant — all hold-up types who can race with some positional flexibility — are best placed to exploit a steady-run race that sets up for a sweeping finish rather than a true test of stamina. This race shape strongly favours runners with a late turn of foot who can sit close enough to pounce off a genuine pace, rather than those needing a strong gallop to be delivered from deep; the field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, with Fanjove, Maldevious, Khabib, Mecca's Symphony, and Lord Abama all true hold-up horses shuffled forward in the map, meaning the genuine closers will be competing for fewer finishing positions than their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Flourish
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the field fans out for home at the 2f pole with finishing speed deciding matters.
scenarios.body: Bay Breeze's solo lead creates a false-pace scenario where runners travelling comfortably in mid-division hold the trump cards; Northcliff and Kings Merchant both carry solid good-ground form and the positional versatility to sit close enough to Bay Breeze before producing a late challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Progressive Type Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the younger or lightly-raced runners with upward form trajectory produces a peak effort on good ground.
scenarios.body: Great's recent win over this exact 6f trip on good turf marks him as the most likely beneficiary if the race develops at a pace that rewards a mid-division mover with a sharp turn of foot; Kings Merchant's 2nd and 1st from recent runs also fits this pattern well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If traffic opens late and one of the deep hold-up types — Fanjove, Khabib, or Mecca's Symphony — secures a clear run through a wall of rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural rearward position due to redistribution, these horses would need the race to slow dramatically early before sprinting home, and even then they face the problem of not being where they want to be tactically; Khabib's four placed efforts on good ground give him the best residual claims if the gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze, though a natural hold-up type placed on the lead, settles beautifully, conserves energy through the first 4f, and proves impossible to reel in.
scenarios.body: At OR 60 and with a history of running close-up finishes rather than dominating, this remains an unlikely outcome, but Tim Easterby's handling of older sprinters in smaller fields on good ground has produced front-running surprises before; only Northcliff's strong finishing kick makes him a threat if Bay Breeze leads into the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Bay Breeze sets the sole pace entirely out of role — if he settles unexpectedly well under Fentiman and uses his redistribution to steal a march, runners sat in midfield expecting a false pace may be caught flat-footed, as there is no genuine rival pressing him for the lead.

Great and Kings Merchant both return quickly (12 and 10 days respectively) in a race where the moderate pace suits their finishing style — if either has bounced off their recent win, they will peak in the straight but may not find the same reserves they showed last time.

Northcliff goes in the visor for the first time and Silvestre De Sousa may attempt to track Bay Breeze much closer than his hold-up profile suggests — watch how De Sousa positions him in the first furlong, as an aggressive move to the front rank would transform Northcliff's chance entirely.

With five genuine hold-up types (Fanjove, Khabib, Maldevious, Mecca's Symphony, Lord Abama) all competing for the same late ground on a 6f flat track, a traffic jam in the final 2f is a real risk — horses drawn wide may benefit simply by avoiding the congestion up the rail.

Mecca's Symphony drops from 7f to 6f where her record is thinner — combined with the gentle pace that denies her a true stamina test, monitor her pre-race market move as a gauge of stable confidence, since Michael Dods runs her alongside Lord Abama and two runners from the same yard in a tight handicap.
